sanskrit: sabale sāgaraṃ tīrṇe rāme daśarathātmaje amātyau rāvaṇaḥ śrīmān abravīc chukasāraṇau
english: When Rāma, son of Daśaratha, had crossed the ocean with his army, the illustrious Rāvaṇa spoke to his two ministers, Śuka and Sāraṇa.

sanskrit: samagraṃ sāgaraṃ tīrṇaṃ dustaraṃ vānaraṃ balam abhūtapūrvaṃ rāmeṇa sāgare setubandhanam
english: "The entire monkey army — so formidable and hard to overcome — has crossed the ocean, and a bridge across the sea has been built by Rāma, a feat without precedent."

sanskrit: sāgare setubandhaṃ tu na śraddadhyāṃ kathaṃ cana avaśyaṃ cāpi saṃkhyeyaṃ tan mayā vānaraṃ balam
english: "I could never have believed a bridge could be built across the ocean; and yet that monkey army must be counted and assessed by me."

sanskrit: bhavantau vānaraṃ sainyaṃ praviśyānupalakṣitau parimāṇaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca ye ca mukhyāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "You two shall enter the monkey army undetected and learn its full measure and strength, and who the foremost among the leaping warriors are —"

sanskrit: mantriṇo ye ca rāmasya sugrīvasya ca saṃmatāḥ ye pūrvam abhivartante ye ca śūrāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "— who are the counselors trusted by Rāma and Sugrīva, who march in the vanguard, and which of the leaping monkeys are the true heroes."

sanskrit: sa ca setur yathā baddhaḥ sāgare salilārṇave niveśaś ca yathā teṣāṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: "Determine how the bridge was constructed across the ocean's waters, and how the encampment of those great-souled monkeys is arranged."

sanskrit: rāmasya vyavasāyaṃ ca vīryaṃ praharaṇāni ca lakṣmaṇasya ca vīrasya tattvato jñātum arhatha
english: "You must learn truly the resolve and might of Rāma, and the weapons of the hero Lakṣmaṇa as well."

sanskrit: kaś ca senāpatis teṣāṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahaujasām etaj jñātvā yathātattvaṃ śīghram agantum arhathaḥ
english: "And who is the commander of that great-spirited monkey host? Having learned all this accurately, you should return without delay."

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭau rākṣasau śukasāraṇau harirūpadharau vīrau praviṣṭau vānaraṃ balam
english: Thus instructed, those two rākṣasa heroes, Śuka and Sāraṇa, assumed the forms of monkeys and entered the monkey army.

sanskrit: tatas tad vānaraṃ sainyam acintyaṃ lomaharṣaṇam saṃkhyātuṃ nādhyagacchetāṃ tadā tau śukasāraṇau
english: But that monkey force was so inconceivable and hair-raising in its vastness that Śuka and Sāraṇa were unable to count it.

sanskrit: tat sthitaṃ parvatāgreṣu nirdareṣu guhāsu ca samudrasya ca tīreṣu vaneṣūpavaneṣu ca
english: It was encamped on mountaintops, in ravines and caves, along the shores of the ocean, in forests and in groves.

sanskrit: taramāṇaṃ ca tīrṇaṃ ca tartukāmaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ niviṣṭaṃ niviśac caiva bhīmanādaṃ mahābalam
english: Part was crossing, part had already crossed, and part still wished to cross; some were settling in camp, others still settling — that great, terribly roaring army.

sanskrit: tau dadarśa mahātejāḥ pracchannau ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ ācacakṣe 'tha rāmāya gṛhītvā śukasāraṇau laṅkāyāḥ samanuprāptau cārau parapuraṃjayau
english: The great and radiant Vibhīṣaṇa spotted those two in their disguise, seized Śuka and Sāraṇa, and reported to Rāma: "These two are spies come from Laṅkā — conquerors of enemy citadels."

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā vyathitau rāmaṃ nirāśau jīvite tadā kṛtāñjalipuṭau bhītau vacanaṃ cedam ūcatuḥ
english: Seeing Rāma, the two were filled with anguish and despaired of their lives; clasping their hands together in supplication, they stood in fear and spoke these words:

sanskrit: āvām ihāgatau saumya rāvaṇaprahitāv ubhau parijñātuṃ balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tavedaṃ raghunandana
english: "We have come here, O gentle one, both of us sent by Rāvaṇa — to learn the full measure of your army, O joy of the Raghu line."

sanskrit: tayos tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ abravīt prahasan vākyaṃ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ
english: Having heard their words, Rāma, son of Daśaratha — he who is devoted to the welfare of all beings — spoke with a smile:

sanskrit: yadi dṛṣṭaṃ balaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vayaṃ vā susamīkṣitāḥ yathoktaṃ vā kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ chandataḥ pratigamyatām
english: "If you have seen the whole of our army, and if you have examined us well, and if the task assigned to you is accomplished — then go freely as you please."

sanskrit: praviśya nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ bhavadbhyāṃ dhanadānujaḥ vaktavyo rakṣasāṃ rājā yathoktaṃ vacanaṃ mama
english: "Entering the city of Laṅkā, you two shall convey my message to the king of the rākṣasas, the younger brother of Kubera, exactly as I tell you:"

sanskrit: yad balaṃ ca samāśritya sītāṃ me hṛtavān asi tad darśaya yathākāmaṃ sasainyaḥ sahabāndhavaḥ
english: "'Whatever power you relied upon when you stole Sītā from me — show it now fully, together with your army and your kinsmen.'"

sanskrit: śvaḥkāle nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ saprākārāṃ satoraṇām rākṣasaṃ ca balaṃ paśya śarair vidhvaṃsitaṃ mayā
english: "'By tomorrow you shall see the city of Laṅkā with its ramparts and gateways, and the rākṣasa army, shattered by my arrows.'"

sanskrit: ghoraṃ roṣam ahaṃ mokṣye balaṃ dhāraya rāvaṇa śvaḥkāle vajravān vajraṃ dānaveṣv iva vāsavaḥ
english: "'I shall unleash my terrible wrath — hold firm your strength, Rāvaṇa! — as Vāsava hurls his thunderbolt upon the Dānavas.'"

sanskrit: iti pratisamādiṣṭau rākṣasau śukasāraṇau āgamya nagarīṃ laṅkām abrūtāṃ rākṣasādhipam
english: Thus dispatched, the two rākṣasas, Śuka and Sāraṇa, returned to the city of Laṅkā and addressed the lord of rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇagṛhītau tu vadhārhau rākṣaseśvara dṛṣṭvā dharmātmanā muktau rāmeṇāmitatejasā
english: "We were seized by Vibhīṣaṇa and deserved death, O lord of rākṣasas; but Rāma of boundless splendor — righteous in spirit — saw us and set us free."

sanskrit: ekasthānagatā yatra catvāraḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ lokapālopamāḥ śūrāḥ kṛtāstrā dṛḍhavikramāḥ
english: "There in one place stand four foremost men, like the guardians of the worlds — heroes, accomplished in arms, of firm and unwavering valor:"

sanskrit: rāmo dāśarathiḥ śrīmāṃl lakṣmaṇaś ca vibhīṣaṇaḥ sugrīvaś ca mahātejā mahendrasamavikramaḥ
english: "Rāma the illustrious son of Daśaratha, Lakṣmaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Sugrīva of great radiance — whose valor equals that of great Indra."

sanskrit: ete śaktāḥ purīṃ laṅkāṃ saprākārāṃ satoraṇām utpāṭya saṃkrāmayituṃ sarve tiṣṭhantu vānarāḥ
english: "These four alone are capable of uprooting the city of Laṅkā with its ramparts and gateways — let all the monkeys stand by idle; these suffice."

sanskrit: yādṛśaṃ tasya rāmasya rūpaṃ praharaṇāni ca vadhiṣyati purīṃ laṅkām ekas tiṣṭhantu te trayaḥ
english: "Such is Rāma's form and such his weaponry, that he alone could destroy the city of Laṅkā — let the other three merely stand by."

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇaguptā sā sugrīveṇa ca vāhinī babhūva durdharṣatarā sarvair api surāsuraiḥ
english: "That army, protected by Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa and by Sugrīva, has become impossible to assail even by all the gods and asuras together."

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭarūpā dhvajinī vanaukasāṃ mahātmanāṃ saṃprati yoddhum icchatām alaṃ virodhena śamo vidhīyatāṃ pradīyatāṃ dāśarathāya maithilī
english: "That bannered host of great-souled forest-dwellers stands eager to fight. Enough of opposition — let peace be made; let the princess of Mithilā be given back to the son of Daśaratha."

sanskrit: tad vacaḥ pathyam aklībaṃ sāraṇenābhibhāṣitam niśamya rāvaṇo rājā pratyabhāṣata sāraṇam
english: Having heard that salutary and courageous speech spoken by Sāraṇa, King Rāvaṇa replied to Sāraṇa:

sanskrit: yadi mām abhiyuñjīran devagandharvadānavāḥ naiva sītāṃ pradāsyāmi sarvalokabhayād api
english: "Even if the gods, gandharvas, and dānavas were to attack me, I would never give up Sītā — not even out of fear from all the worlds."

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu saumya paritrasto haribhir nirjito bhṛśam pratipradānam adyaiva sītāyāḥ sādhu manyase ko hi nāma sapatno māṃ samare jetum arhati
english: "But you, gentle Sāraṇa — thoroughly terrified, utterly routed by those monkeys — think it best to restore Sītā this very day. Who indeed among enemies is capable of vanquishing me in battle?"

sanskrit: ity uktvā paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ āruroha tataḥ śrīmān prāsādaṃ himapāṇḍuram bahutālasamutsedhaṃ rāvaṇo 'tha didṛkṣayā
english: Having spoken those harsh words, Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, the illustrious one, wishing to see for himself, ascended a palace as white as snow and as tall as many palm trees.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ carābhyāṃ sahito rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ paśyamānaḥ samudraṃ ca parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca dadarśa pṛthivīdeśaṃ susaṃpūrṇaṃ plavaṃgamaiḥ
english: Accompanied by those two spies, Rāvaṇa — overcome with rage — gazing at the ocean, the mountains, and the forests, saw the whole stretch of earth completely filled with the leaping warriors.

sanskrit: tad apāram asaṃkhyeyaṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahad balam ālokya rāvaṇo rājā paripapraccha sāraṇam
english: Beholding that vast and boundless, innumerable monkey force, King Rāvaṇa asked Sāraṇa in detail:

sanskrit: eṣāṃ vānaramukhyānāṃ ke śūrāḥ ke mahābalāḥ ke pūrvam abhivartante mahotsāhāḥ samantataḥ
english: "Among these foremost monkeys, which are the heroes, which are the mighty ones? Which march in the vanguard on all sides with great energy?"

sanskrit: keṣāṃ śṛṇoti sugrīvaḥ ke vā yūthapayūthapāḥ sāraṇācakṣva me sarvaṃ ke pradhānāḥ plavaṃgamāḥ
english: "To whom does Sugrīva listen? Who are the lords of lords of troops? Tell me everything, Sāraṇa — who are the foremost among the leaping warriors?"

sanskrit: sāraṇo rākṣasendrasya vacanaṃ paripṛcchataḥ ācacakṣe 'tha mukhyajño mukhyāṃs tāṃs tu vanaukasaḥ
english: Sāraṇa — a connoisseur of great men — then described to Rāvaṇa, lord of rākṣasas, who had inquired so fully, those foremost of the forest-dwellers.

sanskrit: eṣa yo 'bhimukhaḥ laṅkāṃ nardaṃs tiṣṭhati vānaraḥ yūthapānāṃ sahasrāṇāṃ śatena parivāritaḥ
english: "This monkey who stands roaring and facing Laṅkā, surrounded by a hundred thousand troop commanders —"

sanskrit: yasya ghoṣeṇa mahatā saprākārā satoraṇā laṅkā pravepate sarvā saśailavanakānanā
english: "— at whose great roar all of Laṅkā trembles — its walls, gateways, hills, forests and groves —"

sanskrit: sarvaśākhāmṛgendrasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ balāgre tiṣṭhate vīro nīlo nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ
english: "— this hero who stands at the head of the entire army of the great-souled Sugrīva, king of all forest-dwellers: this is the troop-chieftain named Nīla."

sanskrit: bāhū pragṛhya yaḥ padbhyāṃ mahīṃ gacchati vīryavān laṅkām abhimukhaḥ kopād abhīkṣṇaṃ ca vijṛmbhate
english: "That valiant one who goes on foot with arms outstretched, facing Laṅkā, who keeps stretching himself again and again in his fury —"

sanskrit: giriśṛṅgapratīkāśaḥ padmakiñjalkasaṃnibhaḥ sphoṭayaty abhisaṃrabdho lāṅgūlaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: "— he who resembles a mountain peak, his complexion like the filaments of a lotus, who in his excitement cracks his tail again and again —"

sanskrit: yasya lāṅgūlaśabdena svanantīva diśo daśa eṣa vānararājena sugrīveṇābhiṣecitaḥ yauvarājye 'ṅgado nāma tvām āhvayati saṃyuge
english: "— at the sound of whose tail the ten directions seem to ring — this is he who was consecrated as crown prince by Sugrīva, king of monkeys: Aṅgada by name. He challenges you to battle."

sanskrit: ye tu viṣṭabhya gātrāṇi kṣveḍayanti nadanti ca utthāya ca vijṛmbhante krodhena haripuṃgavāḥ
english: "Those foremost monkeys who stand with limbs tensed, snarling and roaring, who rise up and stretch themselves in their wrath —"

sanskrit: ete duṣprasahā ghorāś caṇḍāś caṇḍaparākramāḥ aṣṭau śatasahasrāṇi daśakoṭiśatāni ca
english: "— these are irresistible, terrible, fierce, of fierce valor: eight hundred thousand and a thousand crores of them."

sanskrit: ya enam anugacchanti vīrāś candanavāsinaḥ eṣa āśaṃsate laṅkāṃ svenānīkena marditum
english: "The heroes who dwell on the Candana mountain and follow him — this chieftain hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own division alone."

sanskrit: śveto rajatasaṃkāśaḥ sabalo bhīmavikramaḥ buddhimān vānaraḥ śūras triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ
english: "White as silver, a powerful and terribly mighty monkey, wise, heroic, renowned in all three worlds —"

sanskrit: tūrṇaṃ sugrīvam āgamya punar gacchati vānaraḥ vibhajan vānarīṃ senām anīkāni praharṣayan
english: "— a monkey who goes quickly to Sugrīva and returns again, dividing and arranging the monkey host, heartening the divisions —"

sanskrit: yaḥ purā gomatītīre ramyaṃ paryeti parvatam nāmnā saṃkocano nāma nānānagayuto giriḥ
english: "— he who formerly ranged the beautiful mountain called Saṃkocana on the banks of the Gomatī, a hill adorned with many kinds of trees —"

sanskrit: tatra rājyaṃ praśāsty eṣa kumudo nāma yūthapaḥ yo 'sau śatasahasrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ parikarṣati
english: "— this is the troop-chieftain named Kumuda who rules there as king, he who draws along a thousand hundred-thousands of warriors."

sanskrit: yasya vālā bahuvyāmā dīrghalāṅgūlam āśritāḥ tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ
english: "He whose tail hairs, many fathoms long, spread out along its great length — copper-red, yellow, dark and white, scattered in all directions — this doer of terrible deeds —"

sanskrit: adīno roṣaṇaś caṇḍaḥ saṃgrāmam abhikāṅkṣati eṣaivāśaṃsate laṅkāṃ svenānīkena marditum
english: "— undepressed, wrathful, fierce, craving battle: this same one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own division."

sanskrit: yas tv eṣa siṃhasaṃkāśaḥ kapilo dīrghakesaraḥ nibhṛtaḥ prekṣate laṅkāṃ didhakṣann iva cakṣuṣā
english: "That one who resembles a lion, tawny-colored, with long mane, who stares fixedly at Laṅkā as if to burn it with his gaze —"

sanskrit: vindhyaṃ kṛṣṇagiriṃ sahyaṃ parvataṃ ca sudarśanam rājan satatam adhyāste rambho nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ
english: "— he who constantly dwells on the Vindhya, the Kṛṣṇagiri, the Sahya and the mountain Sudarśana: this is the troop-chieftain Rambha, O king."

sanskrit: śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ triṃśac ca hariyūthapāḥ parivāryānugacchanti laṅkāṃ marditum ojasā
english: "A hundred-hundred-thousand plus thirty monkey troop-leaders surround and follow him to crush Laṅkā by force."

sanskrit: yas tu karṇau vivṛṇute jṛmbhate ca punaḥ punaḥ na ca saṃvijate mṛtyor na ca yūthād vidhāvati
english: "He who pricks up his ears and yawns again and again, who does not flinch at death and does not run from his troop —"

sanskrit: mahābalo vītabhayo ramyaṃ sālveya parvatam rājan satatam adhyāste śarabho nāma yūthapaḥ
english: "— immensely strong, free from fear, who constantly dwells on the beautiful Sālveya mountain: this is the troop-chieftain Śarabha, O king."

sanskrit: etasya balinaḥ sarve vihārā nāma yūthapāḥ rājañ śatasahasrāṇi catvāriṃśat tathaiva ca
english: "All the troop-chieftains who accompany this mighty one are called Vihāras, O king — forty hundred-thousands of them."

sanskrit: yas tu megha ivākāśaṃ mahān āvṛtya tiṣṭhati madhye vānaravīrāṇāṃ surāṇām iva vāsavaḥ
english: "He who stands like a great cloud filling the sky in the midst of monkey heroes, as Vāsava stands among the gods —"

sanskrit: bherīṇām iva saṃnādo yasyaiṣa śrūyate mahān ghoraḥ śākhāmṛgendrāḥ saṃgrāmam abhikāṅkṣatām
english: "— whose great and terrible sound is heard like the beating of war drums by those foremost forest-dwelling lords longing for battle —"

sanskrit: eṣa parvatam adhyāste pāriyātram anuttamam yuddhe duṣprasaho nityaṃ panaso nāma yūthapaḥ
english: "— he who constantly inhabits the incomparable Pāriyātra mountain, ever irresistible in battle: this is the troop-chieftain named Panasa."

sanskrit: enaṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ śatārdhaṃ paryupāsate yūthapā yūthapaśreṣṭhaṃ yeṣāṃ yūthāni bhāgaśaḥ
english: "Fifty hundred-thousands of troop-chieftains attend upon him, that best of troop-chieftains, each with their separate divisions."

sanskrit: yas tv eṣa bhīmāṃ pravalgantīṃ camūṃ tiṣṭhati śobhayan sthitāṃ tīre samudrasya dvitīya iva sāgaraḥ
english: "He who stands on the shore of the ocean like a second sea, adorning and setting in motion that formidable army —"

sanskrit: eṣa dardarasaṃkāśo vinato nāma yūthapaḥ pibaṃś carati parṇāśāṃ nadīnām uttamāṃ nadīm
english: "— he who resembles a split mountain and roams drinking from the Parṇāśā, the finest of rivers: this is the troop-chieftain named Vinata."

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭiḥ śatasahasrāṇi balam asya plavaṃgamāḥ tvām āhvayati yuddhāya krathano nāma yūthapaḥ
english: "His army numbers sixty hundred-thousands of leaping warriors. The troop-chieftain named Krathana challenges you to battle."

sanskrit: yas tu gairikavarṇābhaṃ vapuḥ puṣyati vānaraḥ gavayo nāma tejasvī tvāṃ krodhād abhivartate
english: "The monkey who bears a body of the color of red chalk, Gavaya by name, a man of great energy — he advances upon you in fury."

sanskrit: enaṃ śatasahasrāṇi saptatiḥ paryupāsate eṣa āśaṃsate laṅkāṃ svenānīkena marditum
english: "Seventy hundred-thousands attend upon him. This one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own division."

sanskrit: ete duṣprasahā ghorā balinaḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ yūthapā yūthapaśreṣṭhā yeṣāṃ saṃkhyā na vidyate
english: "These are the irresistible, terrible, mighty troop-chieftains who can assume any form — the best of troop-chieftains — whose number cannot be counted."

sanskrit: tāṃs tu te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi prekṣamāṇasya yūthapān rāghavārthe parākrāntā ye na rakṣanti jīvitam
english: "I shall now tell you, as you look on, about those troop-chieftains who have exerted themselves for Rāghava's sake without regard for their own lives."

sanskrit: snigdhā yasya bahuśyāmā bālā lāṅgūlam āśritāḥ tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ prakīrṇā ghorakarmaṇaḥ
english: "He whose tail-hairs are sleek and very dark, spread all along its length — copper-red, yellow, dark and white, scattered out — a doer of terrible deeds —"

sanskrit: pragṛhītāḥ prakāśante sūryasyeva marīcayaḥ pṛthivyāṃ cānukṛṣyante haro nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ
english: "— as they are raised up they blaze like the rays of the sun, and they trail along the ground: this is the troop-chieftain named Hara."

sanskrit: yaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchanti śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ drumān udyamya sahitā laṅkārohaṇatatparāḥ
english: "Him whom hundreds and thousands follow from behind, united, lifting up trees, intent on scaling Laṅkā —"

sanskrit: eṣa koṭīsahasreṇa vānarāṇāṃ mahaujasām ākāṅkṣate tvāṃ saṃgrāme jetuṃ parapuraṃjaya
english: "— this one, with a thousand crores of mighty monkeys, longs to conquer you in battle, O conqueror of enemy citadels."

sanskrit: nīlān iva mahāmeghāṃs tiṣṭhato yāṃs tu paśyasi asitāñ janasaṃkāśān yuddhe satyaparākramān
english: "Those you see standing there like great dark storm clouds, black as a mass of people, whose valor in battle is true —"

sanskrit: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhān vīrāṃs tīkṣṇakopān bhayāvahān asaṃkhyeyān anirdeśyān paraṃ pāram ivodadheḥ
english: "— heroes armed with claws and fangs, keen in anger, inspiring terror, countless and indescribable as the far shore of the ocean —"

sanskrit: parvateṣu ca ye ke cid viṣameṣu nadīṣu ca ete tvām abhivartante rājann ṛṣkāḥ sudāruṇāḥ
english: "— those bears who inhabit rugged mountains and rivers, O king: these dreadful bears advance upon you."

sanskrit: eṣāṃ madhye sthito rājan bhīmākṣo bhīmadarśanaḥ parjanya iva jīmūtaiḥ samantāt parivāritaḥ
english: "Standing in their midst, O king, with terrible eyes and terrible to behold, surrounded on all sides like a rain-cloud by storm clouds, is —"

sanskrit: ṛkṣavantaṃ giriśreṣṭham adhyāste narmadāṃ piban sarvarkṣāṇām adhipatir dhūmro nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ
english: "— he who inhabits the best of mountains, Ṛkṣavanta, drinking from the Narmadā: lord of all bears, this is the troop-chieftain named Dhūmra."

sanskrit: yavīyān asya tu bhrātā paśyainaṃ parvatopamam bhrātrā samāno rūpeṇa viśiṣṭas tu parākrame
english: "His younger brother — behold him, mountain-like — resembles him in form yet surpasses him in valor:"

sanskrit: sa eṣa jāmbavān nāma mahāyūthapayūthapaḥ praśānto guruvartī ca saṃprahāreṣv amarṣaṇaḥ
english: "This is he: Jāmbavān by name, a great lord of lords of troops — tranquil, obedient to his elders, yet impatient in the midst of battle."

sanskrit: etena sāhyaṃ sumahat kṛtaṃ śakrasya dhīmatā devāsure jāmbavatā labdhāś ca bahavo varāḥ
english: "Great assistance was rendered by this wise Jāmbavān to Śakra during the war of gods and asuras, and many boons were obtained through him."

sanskrit: āruhya parvatāgrebhyo mahābhravipulāḥ śilāḥ muñcanti vipulākārā na mṛtyor udvijanti ca
english: "Climbing to mountain peaks they hurl vast boulders broad as great clouds, and they do not flinch before death."

sanskrit: rākṣasānāṃ ca sadṛśāḥ piśācānāṃ ca romaśāḥ etasya sainye bahavo vicaranty agnitejasaḥ
english: "In his army are many hairy ones resembling rākṣasas and piśācas, roaming about with the fiery energy of fire."

sanskrit: yaṃ tv enam abhisaṃrabdhaṃ plavamānam iva sthitam prekṣante vānarāḥ sarve sthitaṃ yūthapayūthapam
english: "He at whom all monkeys gaze — that lord of lords of troops who stands in his excitement as if about to leap —"

sanskrit: eṣa rājan sahasrākṣaṃ paryupāste harīśvaraḥ balena balasaṃpanno rambho nāmaiṣa yūthapaḥ
english: "— this lord of monkeys who attends upon thousand-eyed Indra, endowed with strength and power: this is the troop-chieftain named Rambha, O king."

sanskrit: yaḥ sthitaṃ yojane śailaṃ gacchan pārśvena sevate ūrdhvaṃ tathaiva kāyena gataḥ prāpnoti yojanam
english: "He who, while walking, passes by a mountain standing a league away by his side, and in the same manner reaches a league with a single upward spring of his body —"

sanskrit: yasmān na paramaṃ rūpaṃ catuṣpādeṣu vidyate śrutaḥ saṃnādano nāma vānarāṇāṃ pitāmahaḥ
english: "— than whom no form more excellent is found among four-footed beings: this famed one is called Saṃnādana, the forefather of monkeys."

sanskrit: yena yuddhaṃ tadā dattaṃ raṇe śakrasya dhīmatā parājayaś ca na prāptaḥ so 'yaṃ yūthapayūthapaḥ yasya vikramamāṇasya śakrasyeva parākramaḥ
english: "He who once gave battle to wise Śakra in the fight and was not defeated — this lord of lords of troops — whose valor in battle equals that of Śakra himself."

sanskrit: eṣa gandharvakanyāyām utpannaḥ kṛṣṇavartmanā purā devāsure yuddhe sāhyārthaṃ tridivaukasām
english: "This one was born of a gandharva maiden by Kṛṣṇavartman, long ago in the war of gods and asuras, for the purpose of aiding the denizens of the triple heavens."

sanskrit: yasya vaiśravaṇo rājā jambūm upaniṣevate yo rājā parvatendrāṇāṃ bahukiṃnarasevinām
english: "He whose Jambū mountain is frequented by king Vaiśravaṇa, that king of mountains' lords, attended by many kiṃnaras —"

sanskrit: vihārasukhado nityaṃ bhrātus te rākṣasādhipa tatraiṣa vasati śrīmān balavān vānararṣabhaḥ yuddheṣv akatthano nityaṃ krathano nāma yūthapaḥ
english: "— ever giving pleasure of sport to your brother, O lord of rākṣasas: there dwells this illustrious, powerful bull among monkeys, who boasts not in battles: the troop-chieftain named Krathana."

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ koṭisahasreṇa harīṇāṃ samupasthitaḥ eṣaivāśaṃsate laṅkāṃ svenānīkena marditum
english: "Surrounded and attended by a thousand crores of monkeys, this very one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own division."

sanskrit: yo gaṅgām anu paryeti trāsayan hastiyūthapān hastināṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: "He who ranges along the Gaṅgā, terrifying the leaders of elephant herds, remembering the ancient enmity between elephants and monkeys —"

sanskrit: eṣa yūthapatir netā gacchan giriguhāśayaḥ harīṇāṃ vāhinī mukhyo nadīṃ haimavatīm anu
english: "— this troop-lord and leader who dwells in mountain caves, the foremost in the monkey host, who goes along the Himalayan river —"

sanskrit: uśīra bījam āśritya parvataṃ mandaropamam ramate vānaraśreṣṭho divi śakra iva svayam
english: "— who takes his delight on the mountain Uśīrabīja, equal to Mandara, the best of monkeys, even as Śakra himself takes delight in heaven —"

sanskrit: enaṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ sahasram abhivartate eṣa durmarṣaṇo rājan pramāthī nāma yūthapaḥ
english: "— a thousand hundred-thousands march with him: this is the intolerant chieftain, O king, the troop-chieftain named Pramāthī."

sanskrit: vātenevoddhataṃ meghaṃ yam enam anupaśyasi vivartamānaṃ bahuśo yatraitad bahulaṃ rajaḥ
english: "That one you see following him, churning about repeatedly like a cloud lifted by the wind, where this great dust arises —"

sanskrit: ete 'sitamukhā ghorā golāṅgūlā mahābalāḥ śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi dṛṣṭvā vai setubandhanam
english: "These black-faced, terrible, cow-tailed ones of great strength — a hundred hundred-thousands of them — having beheld the bridge —"

sanskrit: golāṅgūlaṃ mahāvegaṃ gavākṣaṃ nāma yūthapam parivāryābhivartante laṅkāṃ marditum ojasā
english: "— surrounding the cow-tailed, great-speed troop-chieftain named Gavākṣa, they advance to crush Laṅkā by force."

sanskrit: bhramarācaritā yatra sarvakāmaphaladrumāḥ yaṃ sūryatulyavarṇābham anuparyeti parvatam
english: "Where bees circle all around and trees bear fruits of every wish — the mountain he circles round, equal in color to the sun itself —"

sanskrit: yasya bhāsā sadā bhānti tadvarṇā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ yasya prasthaṃ mahātmāno na tyajanti maharṣayaḥ
english: "— by whose light the beasts and birds constantly shine in that same hue, and whose plateau great-souled sages do not abandon —"

sanskrit: tatraiṣa ramate rājan ramye kāñcanaparvate mukhyo vānaramukhyānāṃ kesarī nāma yūthapaḥ
english: "— there, O king, on that beautiful Golden Mountain, this one takes his delight: the foremost of foremost monkeys, the troop-chieftain named Kesarī."

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭir girisahasrāṇāṃ ramyāḥ kāñcanaparvatāḥ teṣāṃ madhye girivaras tvam ivānagha rakṣasām
english: "Among sixty thousand beautiful golden mountains, that mountain stands supreme in their midst — like yourself, O sinless one, among rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tatraiṣa kapilāḥ śvetās tāmrāsyā madhupiṅgalāḥ nivasanty uttamagirau tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrānakhāyudhāḥ
english: "There on that best of mountains dwell these tawny-colored and white ones with copper-red faces, honey-brown, armed with sharp fangs and claws."

sanskrit: siṃha iva caturdaṃṣṭrā vyāghrā iva durāsadāḥ sarve vaiśvanarasamā jvalitāśīviṣopamāḥ
english: "Like lions with four fangs, hard to approach as tigers, all equal to the fire of universal dissolution, like blazing venomous serpents."

sanskrit: sudīrghāñcitalāṅgūlā mattamātaṃgasaṃnibhāḥ mahāparvatasaṃkāśā mahājīmūtanisvanāḥ
english: "With very long, curving tails, resembling rutting elephants, looking like great mountains, roaring with the sound of great clouds."

sanskrit: eṣa caiṣām adhipatir madhye tiṣṭhati vīryavān nāmnā pṛthivyāṃ vikhyāto rājañ śatabalīti yaḥ eṣaivāśaṃsate laṅkāṃ svenānīkena marditum
english: "Their lord stands in their midst, endowed with valor, renowned on earth by the name Śatabalī, O king. This very one hopes to crush Laṅkā with his own division."

sanskrit: gajo gavākṣo gavayo nalo nīlaś ca vānaraḥ ekaika eva yūthānāṃ koṭibhir daśabhir vṛtaḥ
english: "Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Nala and the monkey Nīla — each one of these troop-leaders is attended by ten crores."

sanskrit: tathānye vānaraśreṣṭhā vindhyaparvatavāsinaḥ na śakyante bahutvāt tu saṃkhyātuṃ laghuvikramāḥ
english: "Likewise other foremost monkeys, dwellers on the Vindhya mountain — their numbers are so great they cannot be counted, though their valor is light-footed and swift."

sanskrit: sarve mahārāja mahāprabhāvāḥ sarve mahāśailanikāśakāyāḥ sarve samarthāḥ pṛthivīṃ kṣaṇena kartuṃ pravidhvastavikīrṇaśailām
english: "All are of great majesty, O great king; all have bodies resembling great mountains; all are capable of making the earth in a moment strewn and scattered with shattered mountains."
